text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's government on Tuesday closed the door to further negotiations with nurses who were fired after going on strike for higher salaries in October and did not accept an offer for reinstatement. The government directed the Salary Services Bureau and the Pensions Office to process their terminal benefits.

- President Robert Mugabe said on Tuesday his government would ensure no one owned more than one farm in the country, in a move towards effectively redressing the existing land imbalance created during Zimbabwe's colonial era.
- A Z$1.6 million urban water quality assessment project was launched in Zimbabwe's capital Harare on Tuesday in the wake of uncertainty over the standard of drinking water in the city.
